notes.title: The "Chums & Chainlinks" Update
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
A huge thank you to all of the players who have already tried the demo, filled out the survey, and even streamed your play sessions! We got a lot of important learnings from all of your feedback and today we've just released an update to the demo! Why don't we walk through our changes together?
[hr][/hr]
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577782/2b75eb34d0f58cbe56eb80de9ec762a2c1f6dc56.gif

 We have restructured the first time user experience (FTUE), and thus have added a save game to track tutorial completion.
Developer Note 
We realised that our main menu, while super fun, was disorganized and a few players never even went through the main tutorial! To make sure people learn the basics, we've added additional guidance to push players towards it at the beginning and barred off the rest of the playground. If you are a returning player that just wants to try the other modes, you only need to reach the first checkpoint; then hold down START to return to the main menu and you should find the barrier has disappeared! :)
 Players can use left and right on the D-pad to adjust the music volume
Developer Note 
The background music can now be adjusted in game; no more having to go in to the system tray because our rocking beats are too loud!

 Added more dummies to the main menu and the tutorial.

Developer Note 
Players have been really enjoying having fun with our test dummies, so we added more! We also restructured the beginning of the tutorial to make sure people understood grabbing before we ask them to climb.

 The Arena now tracks player respawns as a way to keep score.

Developer Note 
People are having a ton of fun racking up knock outs in the arena, so we added signs for each player to show how many times each has been knocked out! As an added present, you will also fine a new weapon to play with on the sides of the arena.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577782/8f6a14d86c14bef467b797b647a7d7f835931745.gif

 A prompt appears at the first launch of the game to let players know they need a controller.

Developer Note 
Keyboard support isn't here quite yet (don't worry we have heard that feedback), so in the meantime to help clear up any confusion we added a prompt to let players know you currently need a controller to play. We also take the opportunity to push players to fill out the survey: it really does help!

 New SFX added for the Sharks

Developer Note 
To help with player feedback when climbing (and for fun) you'll be treated to some new SFX when moving around and climbing with your friends.

 Adjusted the bowling lane to make getting a strike more easy

Developer Note 
Players have been trying really hard to get a strike so we've decided to make it a bit easier. It's still a challenge, but hopefully less frustrating now.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45577782/3e701fddb81f0359146723858b4b3a1c65ec4f03.gif
[hr][/hr]Thank you again to everyone who has tried our demo so far, we hope you enjoy this update!
- The Climbing Chaos Team

notes.title: Climbing Chaos: Sharing The Journey
notes.content:
We're excited to show our work super early, and we hope you come along for the ride.
Here's a compilation of various steps of our journey developing Climbing Chaos.

A Super Early Look
We love these types of games, where physics, teamwork and silly interactions lead to random chaos and memorable moments. This clip shows our early journey and we wanted to share it with you all; Let us know what you think!
[previewyoutube=RR0qUetSURM;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]
 
Weekend at Bernie's Edition
Our gamedev days are full of random ideas that go on the backlog, and then we get to prototype and try them.

This clip shows an idea that gained a lot of energy, "What if the players had to climb and carry a dummy?" Carry a dummy? Like "Weekend at Bernie's"? That sounded fun to us, here's the clip of us trying it as a team for the first time.

All we have to do is climb, carry, pass the dummy around and then deliver it to the shredder, that's all we have to do. Did we succeed in our first try?

Carry the Dummy Feature Approved!
[previewyoutube=RvAsUm_FHZY;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]


Getting Back Into The Fun!
Early on we thought there was something special with "climbing across all directions and ragdolls". Getting a solid sense of control while balancing the unpredictable physics was pretty exciting to us. At the same time, we knew we wanted to include basic ground movement that would allow us to provide moments of rest and another way to navigate levels.

While implementing this ground traversal we got a bit sidetracked and quickly started to miss our "climbing core"; The game felt like just another platformer. Thankfully, we realized this and refocused, and in no time the climbing, ragdoll, and physics fun had returned. 

[previewyoutube=76iO7TXLyzY;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]


Why Sharks?
How our characters came to be, the answer to a question our players typically ask us.

 why sharks?
 why legs?
 we finally explain ourselves

[previewyoutube=p-TBcfJUq14;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Climbing Chaos: Much Earlier Access Demo Out Now!
notes.content:
Grab, climb, and tumble through this early playable demo of a ridiculous physics-based party game! Move your body and each arm independently, climb anything you can grab, even your friends and embrace the chaos with up to four players. Is it too early to show this? Absolutely, but what's the worst that could happen?

Play solo or bring friends for ultimate mayhem.

DEMO FEATURES

A playable main menu with a playground full of physics toys to practice your climbing skills.

Battle Arena
Ragdoll Dartboard
Bowling
Giant Climbing
And more…

 Tutorial, learn to climb solo or with your friends across 2 levels, form chainlinks for the hard to reach places.
 Minions feature, allows players to spawn additional sharks and hot swap in real-time. You can control a whole squad of up to 4 sharks as a solo player or you and your friends can bring up to 16 sharks for a whole lotta climbing chaos.
 Trashketball, dunk dummies or your opponents into the shredder for points.
 Carry The Dummy, you and your team must carry a shark dummy across a level. Grab, toss, swing the dummy. Cooperation and coordination is key.
 Glow Blocks, climb across a level and grab the random glowing blocks for points, first one there gets the most points.
 Infected!, take turns being a survivor and try to avoid the infected for as long as possible to get big points.
 Time Trial, a climbing obstacle race with a series of levels to challenge each team, grab collectibles and reach the end to get points.
 Team Obstacles, a series of puzzles where teamwork matters, work together to unlock the next challenge.
 Team Puzzles, you and your team must carry a dummy to increasingly difficult heights.
 Full couch CoOp and Steam Remote Play Together Supported!
